# OrgPath Runtime {.unnumbered}

::: {.callout-note}
This page is the operator-facing articulation of the **OrgPath Runtime** — the
working software that reads and assesses Active Directory, derives each object's
OrgPath facet values, and writes them to Entra/Azure, then governs them with a
drift loop and surfaces the result in a read-only web console. The normative
sources are the Codebook [UIAO_151](../../../src/uiao/canon/UIAO_151_OrgPath_Codebook.md)
(facet model), the Drift Detection Engine
[UIAO_163](../../../src/uiao/canon/UIAO_163_Drift_Detection_Engine_Specification.md),
and the [UIAO_174](../../../src/uiao/canon/UIAO_174_Governance_Telemetry_Model.md)
telemetry model; the design decisions are
[ADR-078](../../../src/uiao/canon/adr/adr-078-orgpath-attribute-schema-15-facet.md)
(15-facet schema),
[ADR-084](../../../src/uiao/canon/adr/adr-084-phase5-consumer-architecture.md)
(Phase 5 consumer/adapter architecture, incl. the read-only HTTP surface §C7),
and [ADR-038](../../../src/uiao/canon/adr/adr-038-device-plane-orgpath.md)
(device-plane writes). This page describes the runtime that turns those specs
into running software; the [Active Governance](./active-governance.qmd) page
describes the control-plane posture it embodies.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Where this fits — positioning and deployment
This runtime *is* the machinery behind three of the five capabilities that
[Book 18 — OrgPath and the IGA Market](../orgpath-narrative/Book_18.qmd) names
as the differentiated substrate gap: the typed five-class drift taxonomy, the
deterministic 15-facet substrate, and (with cloud-aware transports) the single
reconciled cross-boundary plane. For the command-by-command path that stands it
up, follow the [OrgPath Implementation Guides](../operational-guides/orgpath-implementation/index.qmd);
to run it multi-tenant, see the [Azure SaaS plane](./azure-saas.qmd).
:::

OrgPath is how every governed object — a user, a device, a service account —
declares its organizational position in one canonical vocabulary: *region,
department, division, role, cost-center, classification, hire/term date,
clearance, account-type* (the ten named facets of the Codebook, UIAO_151). The
**OrgPath Runtime** is the software that makes that vocabulary live across a real
estate: it reads the organizational truth out of Active Directory, decides what
each object's facet values *should* be, writes them onto the cloud objects, and
then keeps checking that they still match.

It is a **control plane, not a runtime path** (see [Active Governance](./active-governance.qmd)):
it reads AD and calls Microsoft Graph / Azure Resource Manager to set
attributes, but it never sits inline in authentication, policy evaluation, or
packet routing. Every write is **dry-run by default**.

## The assessment pipeline: read AD → derive facets → write Entra/Azure

The runtime closes the gap between two halves that already existed — a survey
that *reads* AD, and adapters that *write* facet values to the cloud — by adding
the piece in the middle that nobody had: the **derivation** of facet values from
AD attributes.

### 1 · Read / assess Active Directory

A focused directory read pulls just the attributes the mapping needs (identity,
`department`, `title`, office, `employeeType`, group membership, SPNs, creation
date) — either from a **live LDAP** bind or, for repeatable and offline runs,
from a **JSON survey export**. The live read is deliberately thin: it does not
re-implement the full forest archaeology of the AD survey, only the attribute
pull the assessment consumes.

### 2 · Derive OrgPath facets

Each AD object is run through an **AD→facet mapping** that, per facet, names a
source attribute and a transform:

- **alias** — map a raw AD value onto a Codebook value (`"Information
  Technology" → IT`, `"Reston VA" → EASTUS`), exact or substring;
- **date** — normalise an AD generalized-time / ISO value to `YYYY-MM-DD`
  (hire/term dates);
- **derive** — compute a facet from structure rather than a single field
  (`account_type` becomes `Service` when the object carries an SPN, `Privileged`
  when it sits in a privileged group such as Domain Admins, else `Standard`).

Every derived value is **validated against the Codebook** ([UIAO_151](../../../src/uiao/canon/UIAO_151_OrgPath_Codebook.md))
before it is allowed to proceed. A value that does not map to a valid Codebook
entry is **not written** — it becomes a finding instead, so a typo or an
un-mapped department never silently lands on a cloud object.

The mapping ships with a sensible default and is **tenant-tunable** by YAML
override — it is operator configuration, not canon, so you adjust the aliases
for your directory without a code change. (See the *Codebook* reference at
[codebook.qmd](../reference-architecture/codebook.qmd) for the facet vocabulary,
and [where-data-lives.qmd](../reference-architecture/where-data-lives.qmd) for
the authority model.)

### 3 · Write Entra / Azure

Validated facet values are written through the existing device adapter, which
routes by the object's **disposition** ([ADR-038](../../../src/uiao/canon/adr/adr-038-device-plane-orgpath.md)):

| Disposition | Plane | Write |
|---|---|---|
| `ENTRA-DEVICE` | Entra (Graph) | `onPremisesExtensionAttributes.extensionAttribute1..10` on the device |
| `ARC-SERVER`, `STAY-AD-DEPENDENCY`, `MANAGED-IDENTITY-CANDIDATE` | Azure (ARM) | resource `tags` on the Arc machine |
| `STAY-AD-DC`, `DECOMMISSION` | — | skip (no write) |

Writes go out over a real Microsoft Graph transport (httpx + MSAL
client-credentials, cloud-aware for Commercial / GCC-High / DoD), but only when
you promote a run out of dry-run with valid credentials.

## The governance loop

Setting the attributes once is not governance — *keeping* them right is. The
**governance runtime** composes the Codebook, the Phase 5 adapters, and the
Drift Detection Engine ([UIAO_163](../../../src/uiao/canon/UIAO_163_Drift_Detection_Engine_Specification.md))
into a single runnable pass over a tenant snapshot:

1. **observe** the current per-object facet values;
2. **compare** them against the Codebook;
3. **classify** divergence into the five drift categories (Format, Value, Slot,
   Orphan, Phantom);
4. **reconcile** — plan, and optionally apply, the corrective writes.

Each pass returns one report bundling the drift scan, a rollup, and a stream of
**governance-telemetry events** ([UIAO_174](../../../src/uiao/canon/UIAO_174_Governance_Telemetry_Model.md):
`SnapshotCreated`, `DriftDetected`, `DriftRemediated`, `EscalationTriggered`) so
a run is observable, not just a return value.

Two safety rails are inherited from the engine ([ADR-084](../../../src/uiao/canon/adr/adr-084-phase5-consumer-architecture.md) §C5):
**halt-on-critical** stops the line and escalates when a P1 (codebook-integrity)
finding fires, suppressing all remediation; and **governance-review** verbs
(deleting a phantom group, rebinding a policy) are *never* auto-applied.

## The web console

The same data is surfaced in a read-only, Azure-Portal-style web console served
by the UIAO API under `/orgpath` (ADR-084 §C7 — the HTTP surface observes and
analyses; it does not write). Four views:

- **Overview** — drift findings by severity, planned vs. remediated operations,
  halt/escalation status, and a live telemetry feed;
- **Codebook explorer** — the fifteen facet slots, their enumerated values,
  typed patterns, and reserved slots;
- **Principal lookup** — one object's ten facet values with per-facet
  ok / drift / deprecated status;
- **Run governance** — paste a tenant snapshot and view the resulting report.

## Using it

The OrgPath Runtime is reachable from the CLI (see the
[UIAO CLI Reference](../substrate/platform-tooling/uiao-cli-reference.qmd),
`orgtree` sub-app) and as a web app.

**Read/assess AD and derive facets** (offline export or live LDAP):

```bash
# Offline / repeatable — assess a survey export and write the assignments
uiao orgtree assess --from-export ad-users.json --out assignments.json

# Live — read directly from a domain controller
uiao orgtree assess --ldap-server dc01.contoso.com --base-dn "DC=contoso,DC=com"

# Tune the mapping for your directory
uiao orgtree assess --from-export ad-users.json --mapping my-mapping.yaml
```

**Write the derived facets to Entra / Azure** (devices; dry-run by default):

```bash
uiao orgtree assess --from-export ad-devices.json --target-type device --write
# add --no-dry-run (with UIAO_ENTRA_* credentials) to dispatch the writes live
```

**Run a governance pass** over a tenant snapshot:

```bash
uiao orgtree govern snapshot.json --out report.json
```

**Run the web console** (read-only):

```bash
pip install -e ".[api]"
uvicorn uiao.api.app:app --port 8000
# then open http://localhost:8000/orgpath/
```

## The five differentiated capabilities, in the runtime

[Book 18 — OrgPath and the IGA Market](../orgpath-narrative/Book_18.qmd) makes
the positioning argument: five capabilities constitute the substrate gap no IGA
platform — and no composition of Microsoft's own primitives — owns as a primary
function. This runtime is where four of those five stop being an argument and
become running software. The mapping is concrete, not rhetorical: each
capability names a specific component already described on this page.

| Differentiated capability (Book 18) | The runtime mechanism that delivers it |
|---|---|
| **Deterministic 15-facet substrate** | The AD→facet **derivation** step (§2) computes each object's ten named facet values from authoritative attributes and the dual-transport **writer** (§3) stamps them onto Entra `extensionAttribute1..10` and Arc tags — exact, not inferred. |
| **Codebook-validated per-facet enumeration** | Every derived value is checked against the UIAO_151 **Codebook** before it is written; a value that is not a valid enumerated/typed facet value becomes a finding instead of landing (§2). The console's **Codebook explorer** surfaces the fifteen slots. |
| **Typed five-class drift taxonomy** | The **governance loop** (§"The governance loop") classifies every per-facet divergence into Format / Value / Slot / Orphan / Phantom, ranks severity, and halts on critical — the engine, not a generic config monitor. |
| **Single reconciled cross-boundary plane** | The writer and token providers are **cloud-aware** (`commercial \| gcc-high \| dod`); the same runtime reconciles the substrate across boundaries. At multi-tenant scale this is the [Azure SaaS plane](./azure-saas.qmd). |

The fifth capability in Book 18's set — **composable hierarchy with
inheritance** — is the one this runtime *feeds* rather than executes: the
validated facets it stamps are exactly what the dynamic-group / Administrative
Unit / policy-targeting consumers compose against (those authoring adapters are
reserved per the [Implementation Guides](../operational-guides/orgpath-implementation/index.qmd)
scope). The division of labour is deliberate and is the whole ScubaGear-pattern
thesis of Book 18: this runtime owns the deterministic substrate and the drift
fabric; the platform's existing groups, Conditional Access, and PIM compose on
top of it.

> The runtime is not a competitor to the IGA platform above it. It is the layer
> that makes that platform's organizational scoping deterministic — stamped from
> an authoritative source, validated per facet, and continuously reconciled.

## Scope & boundaries

- **Writes target devices today.** Entra-device `extensionAttributes` and Arc
  resource tags are the supported, tested write path ([ADR-038](../../../src/uiao/canon/adr/adr-038-device-plane-orgpath.md)).
  Writing OrgPath back onto *user* objects carries directory-sync semantics and
  is gated on a separate decision.
- **Dry-run is the default everywhere.** Promotion to live writes is an explicit
  per-run operator action requiring credentials.
- **Validation precedes every write.** No value reaches a cloud object unless it
  is a valid Codebook value; everything else becomes a finding.
